newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Thai Airways stops flying to Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways stops flying to Brussels.

text.p: Thai Airways International Ltd has temporarily stopped flying to Brussels, an airline spokesman here said.
Previously, the Thailand-based carrier was flying three times a week to Brussels with a Boeing 747 on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays, he said.
Under its new summer schedule Thai will offer cargo and passenger traffic to Brussels via Frankfurt using its code-sharing agreements with Lufthansa, a Thai spokesman in Germany said.
Flights from Bangkok used to fly into Frankfurt and then go on to Brussels but from the beginning of April they terminate at the Asian carrier's European hub in Frankfurt.

Under its summer schedule, Thai Airways operates a 747-200F between Paris and Bangkok for the first time. The carrier has leased in an Atlas Air freighter for this service which will be operated once a week.

Thai Airways will concentrate its trucking activities on Paris and Frankfurt because its MD 11 five times a week service from Schiphol is nearly always full. Belgian cargo will now be trucked to or from Frankfurt or Paris, the Brussels based official said.
"It is not often possible to put Belgian cargo on flights leaving Amsterdam as they are so busy," he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
